_meta.validation: Two stages per HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING.md section 6. (1) Manual predictions at authoring time (the section 6.5 degraded fallback): predicted recall 10/10, predicted specificity 10/10. (2) The section 6.5 fresh-context agent fan-out is the actual gate and runs natively on any host Claude Code runs on, Windows included -- the abandoned run_loop/run_eval is NOT used (section 6.4), so there is no WSL2/Linux/macOS requirement. Fan-out measured (adjudicated from each agent's reasoning per section 6.5 step 4): recall 8/10 = 80%, specificity 10/10 = 100% -- clears the section 6.3 gate (recall >=80%, specificity >=50%). The two recall misses are the renamed/re-wrapped Reqtificator patch (deferred to modlist memory by design) and the NPC Plugin Chooser 2 staleness case.
_meta.specificity_stress_cases: Negatives 1, 2, and 9 deliberately name tool-output plugins (DynDOLOD.esp, Reqtificator, ParallaxGen) in non-authoring contexts (load-order placement, a failed tool run, a pure CTD diagnosis). They are the queries most likely to over-trigger on plugin-name match alone; watch them closely in empirical re-validation. The description is authoring-anchored ('create a patch, override or forward a record, resolve a conflict, pull a conflict tree, study how a mod works') specifically so these do not fire.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.adjudicator_notes: Skill under test: tool-output-awareness (menu M), description read at .claude/skills/tool-output-awareness/SKILL.md — trigger list now includes ParallaxGen (`PGPatcher.esp`) literally. Recall 8/10 (0.80, at threshold), specificity 8/10 (0.80, well above 0.50) → PASS on both gates. Adjudicated from reasoning per 6.5 step 4; no pick/reasoning conflicts found — every reasoning matched its pick token, so no overrides recorded. Rows 12, 16, 17, 19 correctly answered N with reasoning that explicitly considered and rejected M (12 and 19 named M and gave the right ground for rejection: tool-run failure and CTD triage are not 'what may a patch copy' questions). PRIOR MISS id 1: FIXED — the agent now picks M and cites PGPatcher by name as 'explicitly listed in M's trigger conditions', with no SkyPatcher/PGPatcher name collision anywhere in its reasoning; id 10 (the other PGPatcher row) also hits for the same reason, so the filename addition did its intended job. SPECIFICITY 13 and 19: 19 HELD (N, clean rejection of M); 13 did NOT hold — it flipped from a prior-run pass to a false positive, and its reasoning quotes 'ParallaxGen output, PGPatcher.esp', so the fix that repaired id 1 is the plausible cause of the id-13 regression. Net effect of the change: +1 recall (id 1), −1 specificity (id 13), plus a new specificity false positive at id 11 (DynDOLOD/Occlusion, unrelated to the edit — variance or a pre-existing weakness the prior run happened to pass). Recall also fell on ids 3 and 6, which the prior run scored as hits; both are cross-skill competition misses (skypatcher-authoring's literal 'cell lighting' phrase, and a Requiem domain skill judged absent from the menu) rather than anything the PGPatcher edit touched — treat as run-to-run variance on already-borderline rows. Recall is now sitting exactly on the 0.80 line, so any further regression fails; the shared root cause behind ids 11 and 13 is that M's trigger sentence names tool/plugin filenames prominently while the scoping clause ('BEFORE forwarding, overriding, patching against, or explaining any record') is easy to skip — a future revision could add an explicit non-trigger note (installing, generating, re-running, ordering, or enabling these tools is out of scope) without weakening the filename anchors that fixed id 1.
revalidation_2026-07-28_294.carry_forward: Recall sits exactly on the 0.80 gate and rows 3/6 flip run-to-run: this is the structural cost of evaluating a companion/guardrail skill under a forced-single-pick menu — the deliverable-authoring skill is also a legitimate pick for those queries. Two candidate follow-ups for the next release: (a) an explicit out-of-scope clause for install/generate/re-run/ordering questions (would repair over-triggers 11/13; check against section 3.4's negative-gate prohibition first — frame as a disambiguation sentence like kid-authoring's 'Keywords on NPCs are SPID, not KID'); (b) consider whether the section-6.5 method should allow a stated co-load pick for guardrail-archetype skills.
